information.rules:
# Requirements to be eligible for general prizes

To be eligible for the main prizes, projects must meet at least the following requirements:

- Be deployed on an Arbitrum-compatible network (e.g., Arbitrum One, Arbitrum Sepolia, or another Arbitrum ecosystem chain enabled by the organization).
- Have at least one deployed and functional smart contract.
- Present a functional application (MVP) that demonstrates the use case.
- Submit all requested documentation before the deadline.
- Comply with these hackathon rules.
- Teams of up to 4 members.

> Projects that do not meet these requirements may participate in hackathon activities but will not be eligible for the main prizes.

## Real blockchain usage

Superficial or unnecessary use of blockchain will not be evaluated favorably.

Teams must justify why Arbitrum adds value to their solution and demonstrate that interaction with the network is an essential part of the project's operation, not merely a component added to meet competition requirements.

This helps avoid projects where blockchain provides no real utility.

# Bounties

In addition to the main prizes, there will be bounties sponsored by the Arbitrum ecosystem.

Each bounty will have specific technical requirements published in due course.

Preliminarily, categories include:

- **Advanced:** development using Scaffold-Stylus and AI integration.
- **Intermediate:** development using Scaffold-Stylus.
- **Basic:** development using Scaffold-ETH.

# Project Eligibility

- The project must have been primarily developed during the official hackathon period. The first commit must be made from **July 31 at 4:00 p.m. (KickOff)**.
- Reusing previous projects, libraries, or own infrastructure is allowed only if the work done during the hackathon represents a substantial and verifiable improvement.
- The jury may request evidence of work done during the event (commits, repository history, intermediate demos, etc.).

# Deliverables

### 🎥 Video Pitch
Share a **2 to 3 minute** video presenting the problem, the solution, the project's value proposition, and how it uses **Arbitrum**.

---

### 📑 Pitch Deck
Upload the presentation used during the pitch in **PDF** format.

---

### 🚀 Demo Link
Provide the link to the deployed application or environment where judges can test the project.

---

### 🎬 Video Demo
Share a video demonstrating the project's functionality and main features.

---

### 💻 Public Repository Link
Include the link to the public repository (GitHub or other platform) with the project's source code and documentation.

---

### 📜 Smart Contracts
Provide the following information for each deployed contract:
- **Contract Address**
- **Arbitrum Network Used**
- **Explorer Link (Arbiscan)**

---

### 🏗️ Architecture Link
Share the link to the project's architecture diagram (Excalidraw, Figma, Miro, Mermaid, or other tool), showing the interaction between the system's main components.

# Third-party software usage

Use of the following is permitted:

- Frameworks.
- SDKs.
- APIs.
- AI Models.
- Open source libraries.

Provided that:

- Their licenses are respected.
- Their usage is cited in the documentation.
- They constitute supporting tools and not the complete product.

# Ethical Conduct

The following are not permitted:

- Copying code from other teams.
- Sabotaging projects.
- Unauthorized access to third-party systems.
- Manipulating votes or evaluations.
- Presenting false information.
- Concealing the use of external tools when required.

# Ties

In case of a tie, the jury may consider, among other factors:

- Greater innovation.
- Better use of Arbitrum.
- Greater impact potential.
- Technical quality.
- Demo quality.

# Projects presented during the Bootcamp

Participants who presented an idea or project proposal during the Bootcamp may develop it during the Ethereum Lima 2026 Hackathon.

Prior presentation of an idea does not constitute a competitive advantage or disqualification, provided that substantial development of the project takes place during the official hackathon period.

Reuse of documents, research, prototypes, wireframes, or proofs of concept prepared during the Bootcamp is permitted. However, the MVP, main functionalities, and technical integration to be evaluated must have been primarily developed during the hackathon.

The jury will evaluate the final result presented during the hackathon and the work done in that period, regardless of whether the idea was conceived earlier.

terms.title: Terms and
terms.subtitle: Participation rules, intellectual property, and responsibilities for the Ethereum Lima 2026 Hackathon.
terms.intro: By registering and participating in the Ethereum Lima 2026 Hackathon, you agree to comply with the following terms and conditions. Please read them carefully.
terms.cta_desc: Contact us and we will help you resolve them.

acceptance.title: Acceptance of Rules
acceptance.description: Participation implies full acceptance of the event rules and evaluation criteria. Any situation not covered will be resolved by the organization.

eligibility.title: Eligibility and Teams
eligibility.description: Criteria to validly participate in the event:
items: Individuals over 18 years old.
Teams of 1 to 4 members.
At least one member must be a blockchain developer.
Main organizers and judges cannot participate.

ip.title: Intellectual Property
ip.description: We take your work and its ownership seriously:
items: The intellectual property of the projects belongs exclusively to their authors/creators.
Participants grant Ethereum Lima and sponsors the right to use the project name, screenshots, code, and videos for promotional purposes.
Submitting already finished commercial projects or winners of other hackathons without substantial changes is not allowed.

prizes.title: Prizes and Bounties
items: Prize allocation is subject to exhaustive technical validation by the jury.
A project can simultaneously win a general prize and one or more bounties (if applicable).
The jury may declare a prize 'void' if projects do not meet the required technical quality.

code_of_conduct.title: Code of Conduct
code_of_conduct.description: Ethereum Lima is a safe and professional space. We do not tolerate harassment, discrimination, or plagiarism. Any infraction may result in immediate disqualification.

liability.title: Limitation of Liability
items: The organization is not responsible for technical issues, network outages, or failures in participant deliverables.
Teams are responsible for ensuring their repositories, demos, and videos are publicly accessible before the deadline.

changes.title: Modifications
changes.description: Ethereum Lima reserves the right to modify these terms at any time, which will be communicated promptly to all registered participants.

conduct.title: Code of
conduct.subtitle: Our commitment to a safe, inclusive, and respectful environment for all Ethereum Lima participants.
conduct.intro: We want the Ethereum Lima Hackathon to be an amazing experience for everyone. All attendees, sponsors, mentors, and volunteers are expected to follow this code of conduct.
conduct.cta_desc: Please report it immediately to the organizers.

expected.title: Expected Behavior
expected.description: All community members are expected to participate in a professional and respectful manner:
items: Be respectful, kind, and inclusive.
Foster collaboration and the spirit of building.
Be mindful of your surroundings and your peers.

unacceptable.title: Unacceptable Behavior
unacceptable.description: The following behaviors are unacceptable and will not be tolerated:
items: Offensive comments, discrimination, insults, or personal attacks.
Public or private harassment, unwanted sexual attention, or intimidation.
Plagiarism or deliberate attempts to sabotage other teams' work.

consequences.title: Consequences
consequences.description: Violation of the code of conduct will bring immediate consequences:
items: Verbal or written warnings.
Immediate expulsion from the event (without the right to prizes or refunds).
Ban from participating in future Ethereum Lima events.

cookies.title: Cookie
cookies.subtitle: Information on how we use cookies and similar technologies on our platform.
cookies.intro: For this site to work properly and to improve your experience, we use small data files called cookies. By browsing Ethereum Lima, you accept their use.
cookies.cta_desc: Check our privacy policy or contact us.

what.title: What are Cookies?
what.description: Cookies are small text files that websites save on your computer or mobile device when you visit them. They help us remember your preferences.

how.title: How do we use them?
how.description: We use cookies primarily for functional and analytical purposes:
items: Remember your preferred language (es, en, pt) and UI theme (light/dark).
Anonymously analyze traffic to understand how to improve the site.
Maintain the security of active sessions if we implement authentication.

control.title: Cookie Control
control.description: You can control and/or delete cookies as you wish. You can delete all cookies that are already on your computer and you can set most browsers to prevent them from being placed.

faq.title: Frequently Asked
faq.subtitle: Find quick answers about participation, teams, prizes, and other event details.
faq.intro: If you can't find the answer you're looking for, feel free to reach out through our official channels.
faq.cta_desc: Write to us directly or join our Discord.

questions.q: Is there a cost to participate?
questions.a: No, participation in the Ethereum Lima Hackathon is completely free.

questions.q: Do I need a team to register?
questions.a: You can register individually, but to officially participate you must form a team of 1 to 4 people. We will facilitate team-building dynamics before the event starts.

questions.q: Do I need to know Blockchain/Web3 to participate?
questions.a: While this is a Web3-focused event (Ethereum, Arbitrum, etc.), we look for multidisciplinary teams. You need at least one blockchain developer on the team, but designers, project managers, and frontend/backend developers are also needed.

questions.q: Is the event in-person or virtual?
questions.a: The event is Hybrid. There will be virtual pre-workshops and the building days can be done remotely, although we will have physical meeting points (IRL) for those in Lima.

questions.q: Can I submit a project I was already working on?
questions.a: Already finished commercial projects or winners of other hackathons are not allowed. However, you can build upon an existing project if the functionality to be evaluated was developed from scratch during the days of our hackathon.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.subtitle: At ETH Lima we are committed to protecting your personal information and being transparent about how we use it.
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy describes how Ethereum Lima ('we', 'our') collects, uses, and protects the personal information you share with us when using our website ethlima.com, registering for our events, or participating in the ETH Lima Hackathon 2026. By using our services, you agree to the terms of this policy.
privacy.cta_desc: Contact us directly and we will respond within 72 hours.

data_collection.title: Data we collect
data_collection.description: We only collect the information necessary to operate our services and organize the hackathon:
items: Full name and email address when registering as a participant, mentor, or sponsor.
GitHub username to verify your developer profile.
Web3 wallet address (optional) for cryptocurrency prize distribution.
Skills and track preference information for organizational purposes.
Technical access data: IP address, browser, and operating system (collected automatically).

data_use.title: How we use your information
data_use.description: We use your information exclusively for the following purposes:
items: Manage your registration and participation in the ETH Lima Hackathon 2026.
Send you essential event communications (schedules, updates, results).
Assign mentors, judges, and tracks according to your preferences.
Distribute prizes to winners of the official tracks.
Improve our services and user experience for future editions.

data_sharing.title: Information sharing
data_sharing.description: We do not sell or rent your personal information to third parties. We only share data in these cases:
items: With event sponsors: only name and professional profile, with your prior consent.
With technical service providers (payment platforms, management tools) under confidentiality agreements.
With competent authorities if Peruvian law or applicable regulations require it.
Statistical and anonymous data with the Web3 community to promote the ecosystem.

data_security.title: Data security
data_security.description: We implement technical and organizational measures to protect your information:
items: Encrypted communications via HTTPS/TLS throughout the site.
Restricted data access: only the authorized organizing team can access it.
Passwords stored with bcrypt hashing; never in plain text.
Periodic security reviews of our infrastructure.
Secure deletion of data when no longer needed for event purposes.

cookies.title: Cookies and similar technologies
cookies.description: We use functional and analytics cookies to improve your experience:
items: Session cookies: necessary to maintain your authentication state.
Language and theme (dark/light) preferences stored locally in your browser.
Anonymous usage analytics to understand how the site is navigated and optimize it.
You can disable non-essential cookies from your browser settings.

user_rights.title: Your rights
user_rights.description: As a user, you have the right to:
items: Access the personal data we hold about you at any time.
Request the correction of inaccurate or incomplete information.
Request the deletion of your data (right to be forgotten), subject to legal obligations.
Withdraw your consent for data processing at any time.
File a complaint with the competent data protection authority.
To exercise any of these rights, contact us at: @javierdgtl (Telegram).

contact.title: Contact and data controller
contact.description: The data controller is Ethereum Lima. For any privacy inquiries:
items: Telegram: @javierdgtl (response within 72 hours)
Website: https://ethlima.com
This policy is governed by Peru's Personal Data Protection Law No. 29733.
We reserve the right to update this policy; we will notify of significant changes by email.
